literature.headline_zh: SARS-CoV-2本期文献呈现多方向研究进展
literature.lead_zh: 本期SARS-CoV-2研究集中呈现以下进展。
key_findings_zh: 摘要 连续出现的关注变异株(VoCs)对有效控制严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2(严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2)构成了重大挑战。 [10.1128/spectrum.00217-26]
在2831名住院儿童中,有938名在实施系统性多重PCR检测的中心接受治疗,其中18.6%存在至少1种呼吸道病毒合并感染。最常见的合并感染为呼吸道合胞病毒(39.7%)和肠道病毒/鼻病毒(38.5%)。 [10.1097/inf.0000000000005396]
IPB29在新兴的Omicron亚变体中保持了最强的抑制作用,而IPB24和IPB28具有相同的肽序列,但使用柔性聚乙二醇或甘氨酸-苏氨酸重复连接子。P43在Huh-7和293T/ACE2细胞中表现出优于P37的抑制活性,但在Vero E6-TMPRSS2细胞中则不然。两种肽在阻断S蛋白驱动的细胞-细胞融合方面表现出相似的效力。 [10.1128/jvi.01067-26]
在大流行期间,一些国家报告了头虱感染率和驱虱药物治疗销售量的下降,但这些变化往往是短暂的或虚幻的,对低收入和中等收入国家的影响较小。 [10.1007/s11686-026-01373-3]
RE.2.2的刺突蛋白(S)受体结合域(RBD)对人类ACE2表现出高亲和力。值得注意的是,一些先前无法中和的抗体重新获得了对RE.2.2的中和能力,这与关键的突变突变G446D相关。RE.2.2还在刺突蛋白位点出现了一个新出现的N连接糖基化位点N529。 [10.1073/pnas.2614163123]

papers.title: A bireporter recombinant SARS-CoV-2 Omicron BA.5 for in vitro and in vivo studies.
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT The continuous emergence of variants of concern (VoCs) represents a significant challenge to effectively control severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2). Although FDA-approved vaccines and antivirals have been successfully developed and implemented for the prophylactic and therapeutic intervention of SARS-CoV-2 infection, recent VoCs could escape protection garnered by previous vaccine and antiviral approaches. Determining the efficacy of prophylactics and/or therapeutics against recent VoCs will assist in efficiently controlling currently circulating SARS-CoV-2 strains. We used our previously described bacterial artificial chromosome-based reverse genetics approach for Omicron BA.5 to generate a recombinant SARS-CoV-2 BA.5 encoding a fusion of ZsGreen to Nanoluciferase (rBA.5 ZsG-Nluc) from the locus of the viral nucleocapsid (N) protein separated by the porcine teschovirus-1 2A proteolytic cleavage site. The rBA.5 ZsG-Nluc replicates to levels comparable to recombinant BA.5 wild type (rBA.5 WT) and expresses high levels of ZsG and Nluc in cultured cells. This facilitates tracking viral infection and the identification of antivirals and neutralizing antibodies with EC 50 and NT 50 values, respectively, similar to those obtained with rBA.5 WT. Importantly, in Keratin-18 human angiotensin-converting enzyme-2 mice, rBA.5 ZsG-Nluc retains the same pathogenicity and ability to replicate in the lungs of infected mice as rBA.5 WT. Using rBA.5 ZsG-Nluc, we detected Nluc activity systemically and Nluc and ZsG expression in the lungs of infected mice using an in vivo imaging system. Our results demonstrate the feasibility of using rBA.5 ZsG-Nluc to track viral infections and identify prophylactics and therapeutics against recent SARS-CoV-2 VoCs in vitro , ex vivo , and in vivo . elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 我们使用之前描述的基于细菌人工染色体的反向遗传学方法生成了一种重组严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 BA.5株(rBA.5 ZsG-Nluc),该株在病毒核衣壳(N)蛋白基因位点中融合了ZsGreen和Nanoluciferase(rBA.5 ZsG-Nluc),并由猪睾丸病毒-1 2A蛋白酶切割位点分隔。

elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 我们生成了一种双报告基因重组奥密克戎BA.5 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2株(rBA.5 ZsG-Nluc),该株表达报告基因蛋白,适用于细胞和整体动物研究,并且其病毒复制和致病性与野生型重组奥密克戎BA.5 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2相似。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 我们建立了一个rBA.5 ZsG-Nluc与表达mCherry的祖先严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2株相结合的可行性平台,以同时识别抗病毒药物和针对原始及近期严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2株的中和抗体。

papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 连续出现的关注变异株(VoCs)对有效控制严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2(严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2)构成了重大挑战。尽管美国食品药品监督管理局(FDA)批准的疫苗和抗病毒药物已成功开发并用于严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2感染的预防和治疗干预,但最近的VoCs可能逃逸先前疫苗和抗病毒药物方法提供的保护。确定现有预防和/或治疗药物对近期VoCs的效果将有助于高效控制当前流行的严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2株。我们使用之前描述的基于细菌人工染色体的反向遗传学方法生成了一种重组严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 BA.5株(rBA.5 ZsG-Nluc),该株在病毒核衣壳(N)蛋白基因位点中融合了ZsGreen和Nanoluciferase(rBA.5 ZsG-Nluc),并由猪睾丸病毒-1 2A蛋白酶切割位点分隔。rBA.5 ZsG-Nluc在培养细胞中复制水平与重组BA.5野生型(rBA.5 WT)相当,并且高水平表达ZsG和Nluc。这有助于追踪病毒感染并识别抗病毒药物和中和抗体,其EC 50和NT 50值分别与使用rBA.5 WT获得的结果相似。重要的是,在角蛋白-18人血管紧张素转换酶-2小鼠中,rBA.5 ZsG-Nluc在感染小鼠肺部的复制能力和致病性与rBA.5 WT相同。利用rBA.5 ZsG-Nluc,我们通过体内成像系统检测了感染小鼠体内Nluc活性以及肺部Nluc和ZsG的表达。我们的结果表明,使用rBA.5 ZsG-Nluc可以有效地追踪病毒感染,并在体外、离体和体内环境中识别针对当前流行的严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2株的预防和治疗药物。重要性 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2(严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2),即2019年冠状病毒疾病(新型冠状病毒感染)大流行的病原体,持续进化以逃逸由先前自然感染或疫苗接种获得的免疫力。此外,近期的严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2关注变异株(VoCs)已获得了对FDA批准药物抗病毒药物的抗性。这些VoCs的出现凸显了识别针对当前流行的严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2株的新预防和治疗药物的重要性。我们生成了一种双报告基因重组奥密克戎BA.5 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2株(rBA.5 ZsG-Nluc),该株表达报告基因蛋白,适用于细胞和整体动物研究,并且其病毒复制和致病性与野生型重组奥密克戎BA.5 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2相似。在角蛋白-18人血管紧张素转换酶-2小鼠中,利用体内成像系统可以追踪rBA.5 ZsG-Nluc感染的全身或肺部情况。我们建立了一个rBA.5 ZsG-Nluc与表达mCherry的祖先严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2株相结合的可行性平台,以同时识别抗病毒药物和针对原始及近期严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2株的中和抗体。

papers.title: The α-helix-facilitating amino acid sequence EAAAK dramatically increases the antiviral activity of SARS-CoV-2 fusion-inhibitory peptides via the endosome fusion pathway.
papers.abstract: UNLABELLED: The SARS-CoV-2 fusion-inhibitory lipopeptide IPB29 features a unique design incorporating the α-helix-promoting EAAAK sequence as a rigid linker between the peptide backbone and the conjugated lipid, exhibiting greatly improved antiviral activity compared to lipopeptides with conventional flexible linkers. Here, we characterized its mechanism of action and uncovered several critical insights. First, IPB29 remained the most potent inhibitor of emerging Omicron subvariants compared to IPB24 and IPB28, which share the same peptide sequence but employ flexible polyethylene glycol or glycine-serine repeat linker. Notably, this enhanced potency was abolished in Vero E6 cells stably expressing TMPRSS2, where viral entry occurs via the plasma membrane fusion pathway. Visualization using FITC-labeled lipopeptides demonstrated that IPB29 binds to and enters target cells more efficiently. Subsequently, we generated two unconjugated template peptides, P43 (containing EAAAK) and P37 (lacking EAAAK). P43 exhibited superior inhibitory activity compared to P37 in Huh-7 and 293T/ACE2 cells, but not in Vero E6-TMPRSS2 cells. Both peptides showed comparable efficacy in blocking S protein-driven cell-cell fusion. Although P43 displayed enhanced α-helicity relative to P37, both peptides exhibited similar target-binding affinities. Instead, the cellular uptake of P43 was markedly more efficient, further supporting that the improved antiviral effect is attributable to the inhibition of the viral endosomal fusion pathway. Collectively, our studies provide molecular insights into the antiviral mechanism of IPB29 and propose the short EAAAK sequence as a generalizable strategy for enhancing the efficacy of peptide-based therapeutics. IMPORTANCE: The development of effective therapeutics against SARS-CoV-2 remains an urgent priority. IPB29, a potent broad-spectrum lipopeptide fusion inhibitor currently in clinical trials, requires mechanistic elucidation. Here, we demonstrate that the C-terminal EAAAK motif in IPB29-originally designed as a rigid linker connecting the peptide backbone to the lipid moiety-is critical for its antiviral activity and functions via the endosomal fusion pathway. These findings reveal a generalizable strategy for optimizing antiviral drug design.

The background highlights the urgent need for effective therapeutics against SARS-CoV-2.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study characterized the mechanism of action of IPB29 and compared its antiviral activity with other lipopeptides, including IPB24 and IPB28, in different cell lines such as Huh-7, 293T/ACE2, and Vero E6-TMPRSS2 cells.
analysis.methods: The researchers generated unconjugated template peptides, P43 (with EAAAK) and P37 (without EAAAK), and evaluated their inhibitory activity in various cell lines. analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings reveal that the EAAAK sequence in IPB29 is critical for its antiviral activity and functions via the endosomal fusion pathway, offering a generalizable strategy for optimizing antiviral drug design.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results provide molecular insights into the antiviral mechanism of IPB29 and suggest that incorporating the EAAAK sequence could enhance the efficacy of peptide-based therapeutics against SARS-CoV-2.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's evidence is based on in vitro experiments, which may not fully represent in vivo conditions. However, the results are supported by direct comparisons and mechanistic analysis, providing moderate confidence in the conclusions.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the antiviral mechanism of IPB29, a potent SARS-CoV-2 fusion-inhibitory lipopeptide, and identifies the EAAAK sequence as a key factor in its enhanced activity. The findings suggest that this sequence could be a generalizable strategy for optimizing antiviral drug design. While the study is based on in vitro experiments, the results are supported by direct comparisons and mechanistic analysis, offering moderate confidence in their implications for future therapeutic development.

elements_en.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to elucidate the mechanism of action of IPB29, a potent SARS-CoV-2 fusion-inhibitory lipopeptide, and uncover insights into its enhanced antiviral activity. The background highlights the urgent need for effective therapeutics against SARS-CoV-2.
elements_en.study_design_and_population: The study characterized the mechanism of action of IPB29 and compared its antiviral activity with other lipopeptides, including IPB24 and IPB28, in different cell lines such as Huh-7, 293T/ACE2, and Vero E6-TMPRSS2 cells.
elements_en.methods: The researchers generated unconjugated template peptides, P43 (with EAAAK) and P37 (without EAAAK), and evaluated their inhibitory activity in various cell lines. They also used FITC-labeled lipopeptides for visualization of cellular uptake and compared the α-helicity and target-binding affinities of the peptides.
elements_en.main_results: IPB29 remained the most potent inhibitor of emerging Omicron subvariants compared to IPB24 and IPB28. P43 exhibited superior inhibitory activity compared to P37 in Huh-7 and 293T/ACE2 cells but not in Vero E6-TMPRSS2 cells. Both peptides showed comparable efficacy in blocking S protein-driven cell-cell fusion.
elements_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings reveal that the EAAAK sequence in IPB29 is critical for its antiviral activity and functions via the endosomal fusion pathway, offering a generalizable strategy for optimizing antiviral drug design.
elements_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results provide molecular insights into the antiviral mechanism of IPB29 and suggest that incorporating the EAAAK sequence could enhance the efficacy of peptide-based therapeutics against SARS-CoV-2.
elements_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's evidence is based on in vitro experiments, which may not fully represent in vivo conditions. However, the results are supported by direct comparisons and mechanistic analysis, providing moderate confidence in the conclusions.

papers.title_zh: 促进α-螺旋的氨基酸序列EAAAK显著增加严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2融合抑制肽通过内体融合途径的抗病毒药物活性。
papers.source_body_en: UNLABELLED: The SARS-CoV-2 fusion-inhibitory lipopeptide IPB29 features a unique design incorporating the α-helix-promoting EAAAK sequence as a rigid linker between the peptide backbone and the conjugated lipid, exhibiting greatly improved antiviral activity compared to lipopeptides with conventional flexible linkers. Here, we characterized its mechanism of action and uncovered several critical insights. First, IPB29 remained the most potent inhibitor of emerging Omicron subvariants compared to IPB24 and IPB28, which share the same peptide sequence but employ flexible polyethylene glycol or glycine-serine repeat linker. Notably, this enhanced potency was abolished in Vero E6 cells stably expressing TMPRSS2, where viral entry occurs via the plasma membrane fusion pathway. Visualization using FITC-labeled lipopeptides demonstrated that IPB29 binds to and enters target cells more efficiently. Subsequently, we generated two unconjugated template peptides, P43 (containing EAAAK) and P37 (lacking EAAAK). P43 exhibited superior inhibitory activity compared to P37 in Huh-7 and 293T/ACE2 cells, but not in Vero E6-TMPRSS2 cells. Both peptides showed comparable efficacy in blocking S protein-driven cell-cell fusion. Although P43 displayed enhanced α-helicity relative to P37, both peptides exhibited similar target-binding affinities. Instead, the cellular uptake of P43 was markedly more efficient, further supporting that the improved antiviral effect is attributable to the inhibition of the viral endosomal fusion pathway. Collectively, our studies provide molecular insights into the antiviral mechanism of IPB29 and propose the short EAAAK sequence as a generalizable strategy for enhancing the efficacy of peptide-based therapeutics. IMPORTANCE: The development of effective therapeutics against SARS-CoV-2 remains an urgent priority. IPB29, a potent broad-spectrum lipopeptide fusion inhibitor currently in clinical trials, requires mechanistic elucidation. Here, we demonstrate that the C-terminal EAAAK motif in IPB29-originally designed as a rigid linker connecting the peptide backbone to the lipid moiety-is critical for its antiviral activity and functions via the endosomal fusion pathway. These findings reveal a generalizable strategy for optimizing antiviral drug design.
papers.abstract_zh: UNLABELLED: 抗病毒药物IPB29融合抑制性脂肽具有独特的设计,其中α-螺旋促进的EAAAK序列作为肽骨架和连接脂质之间的刚性连接子,表现出比使用传统柔性连接子的脂肽大大增强的抗病毒活性。在此,我们对其作用机制进行了表征,并揭示了几项关键见解。首先,与IPB24和IPB28相比,IPB29对新兴的Omicron亚变体的抑制作用最强,IPB24和IPB28具有相同的肽序列,但使用的是聚乙二醇或甘氨酸-苏氨酸重复连接子。值得注意的是,这种增强的活性在稳定表达TMPRSS2的Vero E6细胞中被消除,因为病毒进入通过质膜融合途径发生。使用FITC标记的脂肽进行可视化显示,IPB29更有效地与靶细胞结合并进入靶细胞。随后,我们生成了两个未连接的模板肽,P43(包含EAAAK)和P37(缺乏EAAAK)。在Huh-7和293T/ACE2细胞中,P43的抑制活性优于P37,但在Vero E6-TMPRSS2细胞中则不然。两种肽在阻断S蛋白驱动的细胞-细胞融合方面表现出相似的效力。尽管P43相对于P37显示出增强的α-螺旋性,但两种肽在靶标结合亲和力方面表现出相似性。相反,P43在细胞摄取方面明显更有效,进一步支持了改进的抗病毒活性归因于抑制病毒内体融合途径。综上所述,我们的研究提供了关于IPB29抗病毒机制的分子见解,并提出了短EAAAK序列作为提高基于肽的治疗药物效力的通用策略。重要性:开发有效的严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2抗病毒药物仍然是一个迫切的优先事项。IPB29是一种强效广谱脂肽融合抑制剂,目前正在临床试验中,需要阐明其作用机制。在此,我们证明了IPB29中的C-末端EAAAK基序(最初设计为连接肽骨架和脂质部分的刚性连接子)对于其抗病毒活性至关重要,并通过内体融合途径发挥作用。这些发现揭示了一种优化抗病毒药物药物设计的通用策略。

papers.title: Longitudinal antibody correlates of SARS-CoV-2 infection in a US household cohort during Omicron waves
papers.abstract: Background: SARS-CoV-2 vaccines have been updated based on circulating variants and the antibody protection from prior vaccination and infection against emerging variants. We evaluated longitudinal antibody correlates of SARS-CoV-2 infection risk during Omicron waves. Methods: We used data from a longitudinal cohort study from 2021 through 2025 with prospective surveillance for acute respiratory illness and repeated blood collection. A subset of participants also provided weekly respiratory specimens to identify asymptomatic infections. Serum samples were tested using multiplex assays measuring anti-Spike (S) binding IgG and angiotensin-converting enzyme 2 (ACE2) inhibition, a measure of inhibition of the ACE2 receptor interaction, across multiple SARS-CoV-2 variants. Cox models were used to evaluate associations between antibody levels, prior vaccination and infection, and SARS-CoV-2 infections. Findings: Among 119 participants who contributed 438.8 person-years of follow-up, 81 symptomatic SARS-CoV-2 infections and 4 asymptomatic infections (from 33 participants with weekly swabs) were detected. Each two-fold increase in anti-S IgG concentration was associated with a 15% lower hazard of symptomatic infection (hazard ratio [HR] = 0.85, 95% CI: 0.82-0.88). Similarly, each 10% increase in ACE2 inhibition was associated with a 7% lower infection hazard (HR = 0.93, 95% CI: 0.90-0.95). After adjusting for antibody levels, prior SARS-CoV-2 infection remained protective, while recent vaccination was not associated with infection hazard. The peak predicted antibody level after repeated COVID-19 vaccinations was estimated to confer 62-65% protection against symptomatic infection. Interpretation: Higher levels of binding and functional antibodies were associated with reduced risk of SARS-CoV-2 infections across multiple waves between 2021-2025. These findings support the use of longitudinal serologic surveillance to inform vaccine evaluation and future booster strategies against evolving SARS-CoV-2 variants.

papers.title: Sars Cov-2 Variants – Meta – Analysis
papers.abstract: Background of the Study: SARS-COV-2 refers to severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2. It belongs to family Coronaviridae, subfamily Coronavirinae and β genera. Coronaviruses are crown-shaped particles with spikes protruding from their surface. The SARS-CoV-2 genome is a 29.9 kb positive-sense single-stranded RNA molecule containing 14 ORFs encoding four structural and 16 non-structural ones. Proteins (nsp 1-16). Structural proteins include spike protein (S), envelope protein (E), membrane protein (M) and nucleoprotein (N). Non-structural proteins are involved in viral RNA replication and gene expression, forming an RNA synthesis complex in which nsp12 functions as an RNA-dependent RNA polymerase. Unlike other RNA viruses, coronaviruses have RNA proofreading machinery to correct genetic mutations due to nsp14 3′-5′ exonuclease activity. However, it has been estimated that SARS-CoV-2 undergoes 3 × 10–6 mutations per nucleotide per replication cycle Aims & Objective: The aim of this study is to review the spread of current variants of SARS-CoV-viruses. To look at the disease profile of different variants of SARS CoV-2 Virus. To look at the current variants of SARS CoV-2 Virus prevalent in different parts of the world. Methods: A Meta analysis method is used to study about corona virus and its variants. Data was collected from various publications in indexed journals, recent editions of textbooks, website of CDC, NCDC, WHO. Follow by Prisma, at first stage of the search, 280 articles were found, and after reviewing the titles of the articles, 120 duplicate and overlapping articles were deleted and 160 articles remained. In total, 60 articles were removed due to noncompliance with the criteria, the extract of 40 potentially related articles were reviewed, and 50 articles were excluded due to lack of access to the full text articles. Finally, 10 appropriate papers were selected to enter the meta-analysis stage. Results: SARS-CoV-2 spike mutations can increase transmissibility and immune escape, while some recurrent mutations may reduce disease severity. It also finds limited cross-protection across related coronaviruses, evidence of recombination in SARS-CoV, and stronger ACE2 binding that may help explain faster spread. SARS-CoV was detected in 329 of 436 patients, or 75%, and human metapneumovirus in 41 of 335 patients, or 12%; other respiratory pathogens were rare. The macaque experiment further showed all 4 infected macaques shed virus, and 3 of 4 developed lung damage similar to human SARS. Conclusion: COVID-19, a novel coronavirus first detected in Wuhan in December 2019, caused a global pandemic and prompted widespread public-health measures and vaccine development. The outbreak reduced active cases through vaccination but exposed major gaps in pandemic preparedness, prompting calls for stronger long-term readiness.

papers.title: COVID-19 and pregnancy: is a "forgotten" disease still a threat?
papers.abstract: Coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19), caused by severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2), has significantly affected global health, including maternal and perinatal outcomes. Although the acute phase of the pandemic has subsided, the continued emergence of new viral variants, waning population immunity, and suboptimal vaccination coverage among women of reproductive age suggest that COVID-19 in pregnancy may remain a clinically relevant problem. This review summarizes current evidence regarding the clinical course, complications, and prevention of SARS-CoV-2 infection during pregnancy, addressing whether COVID-19 should be considered a "forgotten" obstetric disease. Most pregnant women develop asymptomatic or mild infection; however, pregnancy is associated with an increased risk of severe disease, intensive care unit admission, mechanical ventilation, and maternal mortality, particularly among women of advanced maternal age, with obesity, comorbidities, or without vaccination. SARS-CoV-2 infection during pregnancy is consistently linked with a higher incidence of preeclampsia, including severe forms such as eclampsia and HELLP syndrome, increased rates of cesarean delivery and, in many populations, preterm birth. Vertical transmission is uncommon but documented. Severe placental involvement, referred to as COVID-19 placentitis, may result in placental insufficiency, fetal hypoxia, and stillbirth. Expression of angiotensin-converting enzyme 2 within the placenta provides a biological basis for viral tropism and potential disruption of placental defense mechanisms, contributing to adverse perinatal outcomes. COVID-19 vaccination before conception, during pregnancy, and throughout breastfeeding is safe and effective. Immunization significantly reduces the risk of severe maternal disease, preterm birth, emergency cesarean delivery, stillbirth, and neonatal hospitalization, while also conferring passive protection to infants. Maintaining up-to-date vaccination remains essential for preventing maternal and perinatal complications associated with SARS-CoV-2 infection.

analysis.summary_en: This review examines the impact of SARS-CoV-2 on pregnancy, focusing on clinical outcomes, complications, and prevention strategies. It highlights that while most pregnant women experience asymptomatic or mild infections, the risk of severe disease, ICU admission, mechanical ventilation, and maternal mortality is heightened, especially in those with advanced maternal age, obesity, or comorbidities. The review also notes that SARS-CoV-2 infection is associated with increased rates of preeclampsia, cesarean delivery, and preterm birth. Despite the pandemic's decline, new variants and suboptimal vaccination rates among reproductive-age women suggest ongoing clinical relevance. The findings emphasize the importance of vaccination during pregnancy and breastfeeding for maternal and perinatal protection.

papers.title: Increased receptor binding and spike glycosylation, remodeled immune escape of surging SARS-CoV-2 subvariant BA.3.2.2/RE.2.2/Cicada.
papers.abstract: SARS-CoV-2 continues to evolve. The subvariant BA.3.2 (Cicada), a derivative of the Omicron BA.3 subtype first detected in late 2024, harbors multiple spike protein mutations, ORF7 and ORF8 deletions, and has recently evolved sublineages (BA.3.2.1 and BA.3.2.2), rendering it a critical target for epidemiological surveillance. The BA.3.2.2 sublineage, represented by RE.2.2, shows a marked upward trend in late 2025. Using surface plasmon resonance, we found that RE.2.2's spike (S) protein receptor-binding domain (RBD) exhibits relatively high affinity for human receptor angiotensin-converting enzyme 2, with structural analysis identifying the R493Q reverse mutation as the key determinant. Pseudovirus infection and antibody neutralization assays demonstrated that RE.2.2 exhibited a distinct neutralization profile compared to contemporaneous dominant subvariants. Notably, several antibodies that previously lacked neutralizing activity (e.g., S2K146 and L4.65) to other subvariants regained neutralizing potency against RE.2.2, which was associated with key mutations including G446D. Profiling of RE.2.2 RBD binding to ACE2 orthologs across species showed no significant difference in species tropism from the representative Omicron BA.1. Importantly, RE.2.2 exhibits the newly emerged N-linked glycosylation at spike protein N529 (absent in all other subvariants), a modification potentially associated with immune evasion or spike protein conformational dynamics. In addition, we corroborated the "O-follow-N" glycosylation observation as previously reported, where O-linked glycans preferentially localize near N-glycosylation sites, implying coordinated glycan organization as an extra layer of spike regulation. These findings illuminate the evolutionary characteristics, functional changes, and the constrained virus immune escape of BA.3.2.2 (RE.2.2), providing critical insights into antibody development and variant surveillance.

analysis.methods: The BA.3.2.2 sublineage was analyzed using surface plasmon resonance to assess receptor-binding domain (RBD) affinity for human angiotensin-converting enzyme 2. analysis.summary_en: This study analyzed the BA.3.2.2 sublineage of SARS-CoV-2, showing high affinity for human ACE2 and novel glycosylation. Key mutations, such as G446D, enable immune evasion, providing insights for antibody development and variant surveillance.

papers.title_zh: 受体结合增加和刺突糖基化,重塑免疫逃逸的迅速蔓延的 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 亚变异株 BA.3.2.2/RE.2.2/Cicada。
papers.source_body_en: SARS-CoV-2 continues to evolve. The subvariant BA.3.2 (Cicada), a derivative of the Omicron BA.3 subtype first detected in late 2024, harbors multiple spike protein mutations, ORF7 and ORF8 deletions, and has recently evolved sublineages (BA.3.2.1 and BA.3.2.2), rendering it a critical target for epidemiological surveillance. The BA.3.2.2 sublineage, represented by RE.2.2, shows a marked upward trend in late 2025. Using surface plasmon resonance, we found that RE.2.2's spike (S) protein receptor-binding domain (RBD) exhibits relatively high affinity for human receptor angiotensin-converting enzyme 2, with structural analysis identifying the R493Q reverse mutation as the key determinant. Pseudovirus infection and antibody neutralization assays demonstrated that RE.2.2 exhibited a distinct neutralization profile compared to contemporaneous dominant subvariants. Notably, several antibodies that previously lacked neutralizing activity (e.g., S2K146 and L4.65) to other subvariants regained neutralizing potency against RE.2.2, which was associated with key mutations including G446D. Profiling of RE.2.2 RBD binding to ACE2 orthologs across species showed no significant difference in species tropism from the representative Omicron BA.1. Importantly, RE.2.2 exhibits the newly emerged N-linked glycosylation at spike protein N529 (absent in all other subvariants), a modification potentially associated with immune evasion or spike protein conformational dynamics. In addition, we corroborated the "O-follow-N" glycosylation observation as previously reported, where O-linked glycans preferentially localize near N-glycosylation sites, implying coordinated glycan organization as an extra layer of spike regulation. These findings illuminate the evolutionary characteristics, functional changes, and the constrained virus immune escape of BA.3.2.2 (RE.2.2), providing critical insights into antibody development and variant surveillance.
papers.abstract_zh: 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 仍在不断进化。子变体 BA.3.2(蝉),源自 2024 年末首次发现的 Omicron BA.3 子型,携带多个 刺突蛋白 突变、ORF7 和 ORF8 缺失,并且最近进化出亚分支(BA.3.2.1 和 BA.3.2.2),使其成为流行病学监测的关键目标。BA.3.2.2 亚分支,由 RE.2.2 代表,在 2025 年末表现出明显的上升趋势。通过表面等离子共振技术,我们发现 RE.2.2 的刺突(S)蛋白受体结合域(RBD)对人类受体血管紧张素转换酶 2(ACE2)具有相对较高的亲和力,结构分析表明 R493Q 逆突变 是关键决定因素。假病毒感染和抗体中和试验表明,RE.2.2 在中和谱型上与同期主导亚变体表现出显著差异。值得注意的是,一些之前缺乏中和活性的抗体(如 S2K146 和 L4.65)对其他亚变体重新获得了中和活性,这与关键突变 包括 G446D 相关。对 RE.2.2 RBD 与 ACE2 同源物在不同物种间的结合进行谱型分析显示,其物种嗜性与代表性的 Omicron BA.1 无显著差异。重要的是,RE.2.2 表现出在 刺突蛋白 N529(其他所有亚变体均不存在)处新出现的 N-连接糖基化,这一修饰可能与免疫逃逸或刺突蛋白 构象动力学相关。此外,我们证实了先前报道的“O-随-N”糖基化现象,其中 O-连接糖基化优先定位在 N-糖基化位点附近,暗示协调的糖基化组织作为刺突调控的额外层。这些发现揭示了 BA.3.2.2(RE.2.2)的进化特征、功能变化及其受限制的病毒免疫逃逸,为抗体开发和变异监测提供了关键见解。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 继续进化。亚变种 BA.3.2 (Cicada) 是奥密克戎 BA.3 亚型的衍生物,近期演化出亚分支 (BA.3.2.1 和 BA.3.2.2),使其成为流行病学的关键目标 监测。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究聚焦于BA.3.2.2亚系,以RE.2.2为代表,显示出2025年末显著上升的趋势。研究涉及表面等离子体共振、假病毒感染和抗体中和试验。
analysis_zh.methods: 使用表面等离子体共振技术对BA.3.2.2亚系进行了分析,以评估其受体结合域(RBD)对人类血管紧张素转换酶2的亲和力。进行了伪病毒感染和抗体中和试验,以评估中和谱型和抗体活性。
analysis_zh.main_results: RE.2.2的刺突蛋白(S)受体结合域(RBD)对人类ACE2表现出高亲和力。值得注意的是,一些先前无法中和的抗体重新获得了对RE.2.2的中和能力,这与关键的突变突变G446D相关。RE.2.2还在刺突蛋白位点出现了一个新出现的N连接糖基化位点N529。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 这些发现阐明了BA.3.2.2 (RE.2.2)的进化特征、功能变化和免疫逃逸机制,为抗体开发和变异株监测提供了关键见解。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现对抗体开发和变异株 监测 有重要意义,有助于我们更好地理解病毒的免疫逃逸机制及未来变异株的潜在可能性。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的局限性包括缺乏直接临床结果以及需要进一步验证所观察到的效果。由于研究的观察性质,证据强度为中等。

papers.title: Head Lice: A Revised View of the Impact of the COVID-19 Pandemic on Transmission and Prevalence.
papers.abstract: Background Head louse transmission is a regular occurrence among children when coming into close contact with others during social activities. During the Covid-19 pandemic most countries instituted lockdown periods resulting in isolation of children away from regular contacts, potentially restricting opportunities for louse transmission. Subsequently there were reports of reduced infestations in children at schools, compared with before the pandemic, with a parallel fall in sales of pediculicidal treatments in several countries beyond the longer-term decline in product sales observed over several years before the pandemic. Methods For this narrative review all literature linking Covid-19 and head lice were revisited and re-evaluated. Results Despite the increased opportunity for elimination of infestations, some households with no outside contacts reported persistent incidence of head louse infestation and a review of the various studies suggests that most reported changes in head louse prevalence were relatively short lived or even illusory and in countries with low or middle incomes there was little or no difference in prevalence as a result of lockdowns. Conclusions Some aspects of the social distancing imposed in several countries during the pandemic appear to have continued to have some effect on social interactions of children, particularly in Western countries, with a commensurate slower recovery of head louse prevalence in some communities.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review examines the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on head louse transmission and prevalence among children, focusing on the social interactions and contact patterns affected by lockdowns.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review revisited and re-evaluated all literature linking the COVID-19 pandemic to head lice, using a narrative approach without explicit meta-analysis or pooled estimates.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: There was a reported reduction in head louse infestations and sales of pediculicidal treatments in several countries during the pandemic, but these changes were often short-lived or illusory, with little impact in low and middle-income countries.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review highlights the heterogeneity in reported changes in head louse prevalence, with some households reporting persistent infestations despite lockdowns, and suggests that the social distancing measures had a limited and variable effect on head louse transmission.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Further research is needed to understand the long-term effects of social distancing on head louse prevalence, and to develop more effective strategies for managing head lice in the context of ongoing social changes.

analysis.summary_en: This review found that while there were initial reports of reduced head louse infestations during the COVID-19 pandemic, these changes were often short-lived and varied across different regions, with little impact in low and middle-income countries. Further research is needed to understand the long-term effects of social distancing on head louse prevalence.

papers.title: SARS-CoV-2 Coinfections and Severity in Hospitalized Children With Systematic Testing.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Co-circulation of severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) with other respiratory viruses raised concerns that coinfections may increase pediatric coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) severity, but evidence is limited by variable testing practices. We assessed the epidemiology and outcomes of SARS-CoV-2 respiratory viral coinfections in hospitalized children. METHODS: We analyzed national surveillance data from the Canadian Immunization Monitoring Program, ACTive (IMPACT) COVID-19 study. Children aged <17 years hospitalized with confirmed COVID-19 during Delta and Omicron periods were included. Coinfection was defined as SARS-CoV-2 plus ≥1 additional respiratory virus. Primary analyses were restricted to centres with systematic multiplex polymerase chain reaction (PCR) testing of all admissions with acute respiratory illness (n = 5), while secondary analyses included all centres (n = 13). Associations with outcomes (respiratory support, ventilation, intensive care and severe COVID-19) were estimated using multivariable mixed-effects logistic regression and adjusted odds ratios (aORs). RESULTS: Among 2831 hospitalized children, 938 were admitted at centers with systematic multiplex PCR testing, among whom 18.6% had ≥1 respiratory viral coinfection. Respiratory syncytial virus (39.7%) and enterovirus/rhinovirus (38.5%) coinfections were the most common. Coinfections were not associated with increased odds of severe COVID-19 in centers with systematic multiplex PCR testing (aOR 0.94; 95% confidence interval, 0.76-1.15). In secondary analyses including all centers irrespective of testing strategy, coinfections were associated with increased odds of severe COVID-19 (aOR 1.42; 95% confidence interval, 1.05-1.91). CONCLUSIONS: In centers that systematically conducted multiplex PCR testing, SARS-CoV-2 respiratory viral coinfections were not associated with increased COVID-19 severity. Differences observed when including centers without systematic testing underscore the importance of considering testing strategies when evaluating the clinical impact of coinfections.

papers.title: The COVID-19 Trajectory in Israel: A Comprehensive Analysis of National Surveillance Data on Documented Infections, Test Positivity, and Vaccine-Effectiveness Estimates
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Israel was among the first countries to implement rapid nationwide BNT162b2 vaccination and became a major source of early real-world evidence on COVID-19 vaccine effectiveness. Early Israeli studies reported approximately 90–95% effectiveness against documented SARS-CoV-2 infection, but over relatively short epidemiological periods. This study examines the national trajectory from the pre-vaccination period through the end of the global COVID-19 emergency. Methods Five publicly available Israeli Ministry of Health surveillance datasets were analyzed longitudinally from February 2020 through May 2023. National trajectories of documented infection and test positivity were characterized before and after vaccine rollout, which began on December 20, 2020. Vaccinated–unvaccinated differences were then examined in two ways: first, using routine-surveillance case rates by vaccination status; and second, using an age-adjusted test-positivity analysis among individuals without documented prior infection, with testing denominators stratified by vaccination status. The second analysis, designed to address potential biases from prior-infection history and differential testing, began 19 weeks later, when the required data became available on May 30, 2021. Results The two completed pre-rollout waves declined to ≤10% of their peaks within 32 and 43 days, respectively. The winter 2020–2021 wave, which was already underway when vaccination began, required 68 days. Subsequent major peaks were larger than the January 2021 peak, with Delta 17% higher and Omicron approximately nine times higher. Routine surveillance reached an early apparent vaccine-effectiveness peak of 94.4% in mid-February 2021 and declined to 61.5% by late May, with substantial rebounds thereafter. By early December it was 79.9%, before falling to 37.4% two weeks later and 8.2% by late December; it became persistently negative in February 2022. The test-positivity analysis showed a generally lower trajectory. After unstable estimates during the low-incidence summer weeks, it reached 62.1% in early December, fell to 26.8% one week later and -14.5% the next, and remained negative thereafter. Conclusions These observational data cannot establish causal vaccine effects and do not address protection against hospitalization, severe disease, or death. Within the domain of documented infection, however, the early vaccination-associated advantage attenuated substantially within months and was further reduced when prior-infection history and vaccination-stratified testing were incorporated; in the latter analysis, the contrast reversed by late 2021 and remained negative thereafter. At the population level, national surveillance showed no sustained reduction in the magnitude or resolution of documented-infection waves after rollout. The Israeli experience may therefore be informative for future public-health emergencies, in which early short-window effectiveness estimates may change substantially as population immunity, testing practices, and the pathogen itself evolve.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在分析以色列记录的感染情况及严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2的有效性,利用快速全国性疫苗接种的早期真实世界证据。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究分析了自2020年2月至2023年5月公开的五个以色列卫生部监测数据集,关注记录感染、检测阳性率和疫苗效果在整个人群中的情况。
elements_zh.methods: 通过常规监测病例率和对无记录既往感染个体的年龄调整检测阳性率分析,来研究接种疫苗与未接种疫苗之间的差异,其中检测分母按疫苗接种状态分层。
elements_zh.main_results: 常规监测显示,2021年2月中旬出现了早期明显的疫苗效果峰值,达到94.4%,随后在5月下旬下降至61.5%,之后有所回升。测试阳性分析显示总体趋势较低,估计值在12月初达到62.1%,一周后降至26.8%,接着下降至-14.5%,之后保持负值。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 本研究强调,针对记录感染的早期疫苗效果估计可能会随着时间的推移而发生显著变化,这归因于群体免疫力、检测实践和病原体本身的演变。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可能为未来公共卫生紧急事件提供信息,展示早期疫苗效果估计如何随着免疫力、检测行为和病毒变异株的演变而变化。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 这些观察性数据无法确立疫苗的效果因果关系,也未涉及对住院、重症或死亡的保护作用,因此限制了结论的强度为中等。

papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 背景 以色列是首批实施全国快速接种BNT162b2 疫苗接种的国家之一,并成为早期真实世界证据的主要来源,用于评估新型冠状病毒感染 疫苗的效果。早期的以色列研究报告称,针对记录的严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2感染,疫苗有效性约为90–95%,但仅限于相对较短的流行病学时期。本研究考察了从疫苗接种接种前时期到全球新型冠状病毒感染紧急状态结束的国家轨迹。方法 分析了五个自2020年2月至2023年5月公开的以色列卫生部监测数据集。在疫苗接种开始于2020年12月20日之前和之后,分别描述了记录感染和检测阳性率的国家轨迹。随后,通过两种方式分析了接种疫苗与未接种疫苗之间的差异:首先,使用常规监测的病例率,按疫苗接种状态进行分类;其次,对无记录既往感染的个体进行年龄调整的检测阳性率分析,其中检测分母按疫苗接种状态分层。第二种分析旨在解决既往感染史和检测差异可能带来的偏倚问题,该分析从2021年5月30日开始,即所需数据可用后19周。结果 两个已完成的接种前波峰分别在32天和43天内降至其峰值的≤10%。2020–2021年冬季的波峰,其接种开始时已经发生,需要68天才能下降。随后的主要波峰比2021年1月的波峰更大,Delta变异株感染率高出17%,而Omicron变异株感染率则大约高出九倍。常规监测在2021年2月中旬显示出早期明显的疫苗效果峰值为94.4%,到2021年5月下旬下降至61.5%,之后出现显著反弹。到2021年12月初,该比例回升至79.9%,随后在两周后降至37.4%,到2021年底12月降至8.2%;2022年2月后,该比例持续为负。检测阳性率分析显示总体趋势较低。在低发病率的夏季几周内,估计值不稳定,到2021年12月初达到62.1%,一周后降至26.8%,接着降至-14.5%,之后一直保持负值。结论 这些观察性数据无法确立疫苗的效果因果关系,也未涉及对住院、重症或死亡的保护作用。然而,在记录感染的领域内,早期与疫苗接种相关的优势在几个月内显著减弱,并且在纳入既往感染史和按疫苗接种状态分层的检测后进一步降低;在后者分析中,到2021年底对比结果逆转并持续为负。在人口层面,全国监测接种后,记录感染波峰的强度和消退程度未出现持续下降。因此,以色列的经验可能对未来公共卫生紧急事件具有参考价值,其中早期短期窗口期的疫苗效果估计可能会随着群体免疫力、检测实践和病原体本身的演变而发生显著变化。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在分析以色列记录的感染情况及严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2的有效性,利用快速全国性疫苗接种的早期真实世界证据。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究分析了自2020年2月至2023年5月公开的五个以色列卫生部监测数据集,关注记录感染、检测阳性率和疫苗效果在整个人群中的情况。
analysis_zh.methods: 通过常规监测病例率和对无记录既往感染个体的年龄调整检测阳性率分析,来研究接种疫苗与未接种疫苗之间的差异,其中检测分母按疫苗接种状态分层。
analysis_zh.main_results: 常规监测显示,2021年2月中旬出现了早期明显的疫苗效果峰值,达到94.4%,随后在5月下旬下降至61.5%,之后有所回升。测试阳性分析显示总体趋势较低,估计值在12月初达到62.1%,一周后降至26.8%,接着下降至-14.5%,之后保持负值。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 本研究强调,针对记录感染的早期疫苗效果估计可能会随着时间的推移而发生显著变化,这归因于群体免疫力、检测实践和病原体本身的演变。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可能为未来公共卫生紧急事件提供信息,展示早期疫苗效果估计如何随着免疫力、检测行为和病毒变异株的演变而变化。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 这些观察性数据无法确立疫苗的效果因果关系,也未涉及对住院、重症或死亡的保护作用,因此限制了结论的强度为中等。

papers.title: Using large language models to facilitate literature review and data extraction for infectious disease models: COVID-19 as a test case
papers.abstract: Infectious disease transmission models are governed by parameters informed by systematic review of epidemiological literature. Large language models (LLMs) could facilitate this, but the reliability of the results to inform models has not been tested. We built an open-source, end-to-end pipeline to simulate LLM performance in a hypothetical scenario where they were available to inform COVID-19 models developed during the first four months of 2020. It screened articles and extracted the reproduction number, serial interval, and incubation period from full-text PDFs. We applied it to 2,067 PubMed/medRxiv records published 31 December 2019–30 April 2020 using four models (GPT-5-mini, GPT-5.4, Claude Opus 4.8 and Gemini 2.5 Pro) and evaluated it against full-corpus human screening and 50-article extraction gold standards. We combined models post hoc, pooled the extracted values into an infectious disease (SEIR) model, and ran sensitivity analyses to test approaches to improve extraction accuracy. Screening sensitivity was 0.72-0.95 and specificity 0.92-0.99. For articles reporting few values, extraction F1 was 0.90-0.96 with precision 0.91-1.00; across all articles, including those with dozens of stratified estimates, recall fell to 0.38-0.78. No fabricated values observed; errors were misassignments of values filed under the wrong parameter, or borrowed values treated as the study’s own. Incomplete extraction from dense articles was mainly due to prompting and output format, not model capability. Ensembling allowed recall-precision trade-offs, and correctness increased with model agreement, from about 30% at one vote to 92-95% at four. The pipeline processed the corpus in hours versus an estimated 130-265 person-hours of manual effort. Our results show that current models can extract transmission parameters from unstructured literature accurately enough to inform outbreak modelling. The bottleneck lies in task specification, and careful prompt and output schema design are key to reducing misassignment errors. Human effort is best directed at workflow development and provenance validation.

analysis.summary_en: This review explores the use of large language models (LLMs) to extract epidemiological parameters from literature to inform infectious disease models, using SARS-CoV-2 as a test case. The study developed an open-source pipeline to simulate LLM performance in a hypothetical scenario where they were used to inform models during the early stages of the pandemic. The pipeline extracted key parameters such as reproduction number, serial interval, and incubation period from 2,067 articles published between December 2019 and April 2020. The results showed that LLMs could extract transmission parameters with sufficient accuracy to inform outbreak modeling, though challenges remained in task specification and reducing misassignment errors. The authors emphasize the importance of careful prompt and output schema design, as well as human validation in workflow development. The study highlights the potential of LLMs in accelerating literature review and data extraction processes for infectious disease modeling.

papers.title: Outcomes of immunocompromised and non-immunocompromised patients in the ICU diverge late in the pandemic.
papers.abstract: RATIONALE: The impact of immunocompromising conditions on outcomes in critically ill patients with COVID-19 remains poorly characterized. We hypothesized that disparities in COVID-19 outcomes in immunocompromised patients may differ by viral strain and time course of the pandemic. METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed SARS-CoV-2 RT-PCR positive patients admitted to intensive care (ICU) at Stanford from March 2020 to July 2022 using electronic medical records. Immunocompromised status included solid organ transplant; hematologic malignancy/transplant; solid cancer with metastases and recent chemotherapy; HIV/AIDS; and connective tissue disease on immunosuppression. SARS-CoV-2 strain periods were classified as pre-Delta (3/2020-8/2021), Delta (9/2021-12/2021), and Omicron (1/2022-7/2022). We assessed 90-day survival differences between immunocompromised and non-immunocompromised patients by strain using Cox-proportional hazards, adjusted for age, sex, and APACHE II score. RESULTS: A total of 791 patients were included, 450 from the pre-Delta period, 114 from the Delta period, and 227 from the Omicron period. We compared 633 non-immunocompromised patients with 158 immunocompromised patients (77 during the pre-Delta, 22 Delta, and 59 Omicron periods). Patients admitted during the Omicron period were more likely to be immunocompromised (26%) compared to pre-Delta (17%) or Delta periods (19%; p = 0.008). Immunocompromise was associated with worse outcomes in the entire cohort after adjustment (HR 1.68, 95% CI 1.2-2.3, p < 0.001). However, when stratified by strain period, immunocompromised status was only significantly associated with higher 90-day mortality in patients from the Omicron period (42% vs 17%, HR 2.9, CI% 1.7-5.0, p < 0.001). Differences in mortality between immunocompromised and immunocompetent patients were not statistically different in either the pre-Delta (34% vs. 23%, HR 1.4, 95% CI 0.9-2.1, p = 0.15) or Delta periods (32% vs. 28% HR 1.0, 95% CI 0.4-2.5, p = 0.92). Notably, survival was significantly improved during the Omicron period compared to earlier strain periods in immunocompetent patients (HR 0.6, 95% CI 0.4-0.9, p = 0.02) but not for immunocompromised patients (HR 1.4, 95% CI 0.80-2.44, p = 0.24). CONCLUSION: In this retrospective cohort analysis of patients admitted to the ICU due to SARS-CoV-2 infection, we found that lower survival among immunocompromised patients was due to higher mortality during the Omicron period, with similar mortality between immunocompetent and immunocompromised patients during other periods.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 该研究探讨了在严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2大流行的不同阶段,免疫功能受损和免疫功能正常的ICU患者结局,重点关注这些结局随时间的变化情况。核心问题是免疫功能受损状态是否在不同病毒株时期(特别是Delta前、Delta和Omicron时期)对死亡率率产生不同的影响。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 这项回顾性分析是针对2020年3月至2022年7月期间被收治在斯坦福大学重症监护病房(ICU)的队列研究 RT-PCR阳性患者的回顾性分析。研究使用电子病历,并将严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2毒株时期分为三个阶段:Delta前(2020年3月至2021年8月)、Delta(2021年9月至2021年12月)和Omicron(2022年1月至2022年7月)。免疫功能低下状态的定义基于诸如实体器官移植、血液系统恶性肿瘤/移植、伴有转移的实体癌及近期化疗、HIV/AIDS以及免疫抑制的结缔组织疾病等条件。分析采用Cox比例风险模型评估90天生存率差异,并调整年龄、性别和APACHE II评分。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 该研究发现,免疫功能低下患者总体预后较差,其风险比为1.68(95% CI 1.2-2.3,p < 0.001)。然而,当按病毒株时期分层分析时,免疫功能低下状态仅在奥密克戎时期与更高的90天死亡率显著相关(42% vs 17%,HR 2.9,CI 1.7-5.0,p < 0.001)。相比之下,在Delta变异株出现前和Delta时期,免疫功能低下与非免疫功能低下患者之间的死亡率无显著差异。值得注意的是,与之前时期相比,免疫功能正常患者在奥密克戎时期生存率有所改善,但这种改善在免疫功能低下患者中并未观察到。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 该研究承认,免疫功能低下状态与死亡率之间的关联并非在所有病毒株时期都一致。具体而言,在新冠Delta变异株之前和Delta变异株时期,免疫功能低下患者与非免疫功能低下患者在死亡率方面的差异并不具有统计学意义。这表明病毒株和疫情时间线可能导致结果的异质性。此外,该研究未提供关于观察到的死亡率差异的潜在机制,或在Omicron时期免疫功能正常患者生存率提高的具体因素的信息。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 这些发现强调了需要进一步研究以了解免疫功能低下患者在疫情不同阶段出现不同结果的机制。它还突显了持续进行监测以及为免疫功能低下人群制定针对性干预措施的重要性,尤其是在奥密克戎时期。未来的研究应探讨特定病毒变异株的影响以及免疫抑制治疗在影响患者结果中的作用。
